approach: Add one integration test, crates/athena-core/tests/buy_first.rs, that ties the root Cargo.toml `[workspace.dependencies]` external crates (entries with no `path` key, parsed with the existing `toml_edit` dependency) to the Decision bullets of every decision headed "Buy before build" (D36 plus one new appended entry). A crate counts as recorded only as an exact backticked name inside such a Decision bullet. Append a new decision that records proc-macro2, syn and toml_edit with the unmet need for each; D36 stays unedited because the log is append-only. The new entry avoids the phrases the backtest parser reads (`superseded by`, `supersedes`, `amends`), so docs/decision-links.toml needs no change (Option B). The spec test uses the production `parse_spec`, `spec_gaps` and `measure_problem`, plus two pure helpers in the test file, `owner_problem` and `measure_label_problem`, because `measure_problem` accepts `status: requirement`. Then fill the spec entry, add the shard-timings line that ci_shards requires, and add a CHANGELOG line. Cargo.toml, crates/*/src and crates/athena-core/Cargo.toml do not change.

decisions.choice: Count a crate as recorded only when it is an exact backticked name in the `- **Decision:**` bullet of an entry whose heading contains 'Buy before build'. The bullet runs from the line starting `- **Decision:**` up to the next line starting `- **` at column 0 (D36's bullet spans nested lines 808-823).
decisions.reason: docs/decisions.md lines 824-828 name chrono, time, reqwest, ureq, tiktoken-rs and proptest as backticked turned-down options. A whole-entry search would pass an adopted crate the record rejects. Limiting the search to the Decision bullet keeps the check true to 'adopted'.

rejected.option: Search the whole text of every Buy-before-build entry
rejected.why: Passes a crate the record turned down.

decisions.choice: Append a new decision after D172 (heading line 4968; the producer re-reads the last id at write time and uses the next, D173 in the base). Heading: `## D<next> · Buy before build: syn, proc-macro2 and toml_edit are adopted, and a test ties the dependency list to the record`. The test keys on the heading text, not the number. The entry adds to D36's record without using the phrases `superseded by`, `supersedes` or `amends` (any case), and says only that D36 is unchanged and the test reads D36 and this entry together.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3 (Option B). crates/athena-cli/src/backtest.rs lines 78-81 parse those three phrases, and the real-log test in crates/athena-cli/tests/backtest.rs fails on a hit with no [[link]] in docs/decision-links.toml. Avoiding the phrases means no link is parsed, no governance file changes, and D36 stays active, which is true: its adoptions stand. mirrors.rs forbids editing D36.

rejected.option: State 'Amends D36' and add a [[link]] to docs/decision-links.toml
rejected.why: Option A is more formal, but it adds a data file outside the brief's deliverables, and the new entry does not change any D36 adoption. It only fills a gap.

rejected.option: Edit D36's Decision bullet in place
rejected.why: Refused by the append-only rule in crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs.

decisions.choice: Add pure helpers `owner_problem(&SpecRequirement) -> Option<String>` and `measure_label_problem(&SpecRequirement) -> Option<String>` in buy_first.rs. `measure_label_problem` returns Some unless the measure ends with `status: not shown` and contains `cargo test -p athena-core --test buy_first`. The spec test also calls production `parse_spec`, `spec_gaps` and `measure_problem` (hestia.rs 1172, 1291, 1219).
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. `status: requirement` is in STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS (status.rs line 321), so `measure_problem` returns None for it (hestia.rs 1229-1234). No production function enforces 'ends with status: not shown', so the test supplies that check itself. The wrong-label negative asserts `measure_label_problem` is Some for `status: requirement`. A separate negative sets `status: bogus` and asserts the production `measure_problem` is Some. `spec_gaps` ignores the owner, hence `owner_problem`.

rejected.option: Assert 'measure_problem is Some, or the end-label assertion fails'
rejected.why: A test cannot assert that an assertion fails, and measure_problem accepts `status: requirement`.
Can disagree with the production parse on multi-line or single-quoted values.

decisions.choice: Disclose the limits in the spec mechanism text and in the new decision's Tradeoff. (a) Only the root `[workspace.dependencies]` is checked; a member crate adding `foo = "1"` directly in its own manifest bypasses it. (b) The check is one-way: it keys on the heading text and does not follow later reversals, so a crate whose adoption was later dropped stays counted, and an entry for a crate no longer in Cargo.toml is not flagged. (c) Whether a maintained option exists stays the verifier's judgement. Add a test that an entry with a matching heading but no Decision bullet records nothing.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. Skipping superseded entries needs decisions.rs status, which is a larger design than the request. Disclosure plus a test that the heading alone proves nothing is the smallest honest design. Auditing member manifests is out of scope in the brief.

rejected.option: Skip entries that decisions.rs reports as superseded
rejected.why: Pulls athena-cli parsing into an athena-core test; athena-core does not depend on athena-cli.
